entities.summary:
Niccolò Perotti, also Perotto or Nicolaus Perottus, was an Italian humanist who authored one of the first modern Latin school grammars, 'De ratione dictendi et dictaminis'.

Born in the late 15th century in Ferrara, Italy, Perotti was educated at the University of Bologna, where he studied law, medicine, and philosophy. His work on Latin grammar influenced the development of the Renaissance humanist movement.

Perotti's most famous work, 'De ratione dictendi et dictaminis', was published in 1477 and became a standard reference for Latin language and grammar. The book's emphasis on the importance of Latin in education and its use in legal and literary contexts helped establish Latin as a central language of the Renaissance.

Perotti's legacy can be seen in the work of later humanists, such as Erasmus and Montaigne, who built upon his ideas about the role of language and education in shaping human culture. His contributions to the development of Latin grammar and language also had a lasting impact on the study of classical languages and literature.

Perotto's grammatical work 'De ratione dictendi et dictaminis' is still studied by scholars today for its insights into the language and culture of the Renaissance.

The significance of Perotto's work lies in its role in shaping the Renaissance humanist movement and its enduring influence on the study of Latin language and grammar.

Niccolò Perotti, also Perotto or Nicolaus Perottus, was an Italian humanist and the author of one of the first modern Latin school grammars.

Born in 1429 in Sassoferrato, Italy, Perotti was a prominent figure in the Renaissance humanist movement, which sought to revive classical Greek and Roman knowledge.

Perotti's most notable contribution was his grammar book, which was widely used in schools and universities across Europe.

Perotti's work had a significant impact on the development of modern language education, and his influence can still be seen in language curricula today.

Perotti's legacy extends beyond his grammatical work, as he was also a patron of the arts and a collector of rare manuscripts.

One of the most striking aspects of Perotti's life is the fact that he was a key figure in the revival of interest in classical learning during the Renaissance.

In his later years, Perotti suffered from a debilitating illness, which left him unable to continue his work.

Despite his limitations, Perotti remained a prominent figure in intellectual circles until his death in 1480.

Perotti's work continues to be studied and admired by scholars today, who recognize his contributions to the development of modern language education.
